idiom_name: plain object literal + JSON.stringify/parse (structuredClone for in-process copies)
implementation_notes: JavaScript's DTO is a plain object literal: no class, no accessors, and JSON - the language's native serialization format - is built in, so the classic bean and its serializer disappear entirely. A toJSON method or a replacer is the hook when an object must not serialize verbatim, and structuredClone deep-copies a value for in-process boundaries using the structured clone algorithm. What is not replaced is validation or typing: JSON.parse returns an untyped value, so an untrusted payload must be schema-checked before it is treated as the DTO.
pitfalls: JSON.stringify silently drops functions, undefined and symbol-valued properties, throws on circular references, turns Date into a string and Map/Set into {} - every non-JSON type needs an explicit convention.
There is no runtime type: JSON.parse returns a fully untyped value, so a typo in a consumer never fails at the boundary.
Prototype pollution: parsing attacker-controlled JSON with keys such as __proto__ and merging it into objects can corrupt prototypes - validate keys, or use Object.create(null)/Map where appropriate.
